headline: Denied floodplain application for addition at 15 Hardwick Road; scheduled September 16 public hearings on wetlands applications 2074, 2075 and 2076.
summary: Denied Floodplain Application #26-466F-317 for an addition to a home at 15 Hardwick Road without prejudice, after the Director of Public Works said the submitted drawing did not address concerns. Set September 16 public hearings and site walks for Applications 2074 and 2075 (Flex Storage Building, East Main Street) and 2076 (drainage pipe, Collins Road). Continued Floodplain Application #26-467F-318, for the East Main Street building, to October 5.
decisions: Approved minutes of the July 6, 2026 regular meeting, as amended, 7-0.
Received Application #2074 for a Flex Storage Building on East Main Street, 7-0.
Received Application #2075 for a Flex Storage Building on East Main Street, 7-0.
Received Floodplain Application #26-467F-318 for a Flex Storage Building on East Main Street, 7-0.
Scheduled a public hearing with site walk on September 16 at 5:30 p.m. for Application #2074, 7-0.
Declared Application #2075 a significant activity and scheduled a public hearing with site walk on September 16 at 5:30 p.m., 7-0.
Continued Floodplain Application #26-467F-318 to the October 5 meeting, 7-0.
Received Application #2076 for a new drainage pipe from Collins Road, 7-0.
Declared Application #2076 a significant activity and scheduled a public hearing with site walk on September 16 at 5:00 p.m., 7-0.
Denied Floodplain Application #26-466F-317 for an addition at 15 Hardwick Road without prejudice, 7-0.
Filed the Inland Wetlands enforcement officer reports dated June 30 and August 28, 2026, 6-1, with Commissioner Robinson opposed.

Bristol Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency Regular Meeting of September 2nd, 2026 
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
 
 
 
 
– 1 – 
 
 
INLAND WETLANDS & WATERCOURSES AGENCY  
OF THE CONSERVATION COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF BRISTOL 
MINUTES 
REGULAR MEETING OF WEDNESDAY SEPTEMBER 2, 2026 
 
By: Chairman Rooks  Time: 6:30 P.M.  Place: City Hall 
       Council Chambers 
       111 North Main St. 
       First Floor 
ROLL CALL: 
 
MEMBERS NAME: PRESENT ABSENT 
    
REGULAR MEMBERS David Rooks (Chairman) X  
 Michael Robinson (Vice Chairman) X  
 Daniel Massaro, Jr. (Secretary) X  
 James Carros  X 
 Laura Valentino X  
 Greg Klimek X  
 Faye Duquette X  
    
ALTERNAME MEMBERS Joseph Longo 
 
X 
 Justin Bridges X  
 Erik Jarboe X  
  
 
 
STAFF Raymond Rogozinski, P.E. Director of Public Works X   
   
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Per the order of Chairman Rooks, the meeting was called to order at 6:30 P.M. 
 
Chairman Rooks designated regular Commissioners Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks with 
alternates Bridges and Jarboe alternating to vote for each application. 
 
2. Pledge of Allegiance 
 
3. Public Participation 
 
None 
 
4. Approval of Minutes 
 
a. Regular Meeting – July 6, 2026 
 
MOTION: Move to approve minutes of the July 6, 2026, regular meeting, as amended. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Massaro 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Bridges, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
 
5. Receipt of New Applications
Bristol Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency Regular Meeting of September 2nd, 2026 
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
 
 
 
 
– 2 – 
 
 
 
a. Application 2074 — Wetlands boundary change for the development of a Flex Storage Building consisting of 
12, 250 sq. ft. at Map 41, Lot 34+33A East Main Street; Assessor's Map 41, Lot 34+33A; Thirty-Three 
Thirty-Four Associates, LLC, applicant/owner. 
 
b. Application 2075 — Wetlands application for the development of a Flex Storage Building consisting of 12, 
250 sq. ft. at Map 41, Lot 34+33A East Main Street; Assessor's Map 41, Lot 34+33A; Thirty-Three Thirty-
Four Associates, LLC, applicant/owner. 
 
c. Application #26-467F-318 — Floodplain Application for the development of a Flex Storage Building 
consisting of 12,250 sq. ft. at Map 41, Lot 34+33A East Main Street; Assessor's Map 41, Lot 34+33A; Thirty-
Three Thirty-Four Associates, LLC, applicant/owner. 
 
Chairman Rooks explained Applications #2074, #2075 and # 26-467F-318 would be heard concurrently but voted on 
separately.  
 
The Agency received the following items in their electronic packets:  
 
a. Assessor’s Map with Inland Wetlands Watercourse Layers 
b. FEMA Mapping 
c. Application 
d. Stormwater Report, from Cole, Civil Survey, dated June 23, 2025 
e. Plan (Electronic Copy Only) 
 
MOTION: Move to receive Application #2074. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Robinson 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Jarboe, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is received.  
 
MOTION: Move to receive Application #2075. 
 
By: Robinson Seconded: Klimek 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Bridges, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is received.  
 
MOTION: Move to receive Application #26-467F-318. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Robinson 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Jarboe, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, shared an email from Attorney Ziogas stating he requested a 
public hearing be set for the October 5th Meeting.
Bristol Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency Regular Meeting of September 2nd, 2026 
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
 
 
 
 
– 3 – 
 
 
 
MOTION: Move to schedule a Public Hearing with site walk on September 16th 5:30 pm for Application 
#2074.  
 
By: Massaro Seconded: Klimek 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Bridges, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application was submitted for a public hearing 
 
 
MOTION: Move to declare Application #2075 a significant activity and schedule a Public Hearing with site 
walk on September 16th 5:30 pm. 
 
By: Massaro Seconded: Robinson 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Jarboe, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application was declared a significant activity. 
 
 
MOTION: Move to continue Application #26-467F-318 to the October 5th, meeting. 
 
By: Robinson Seconded: Klimek 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Bridges, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application was continued. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
d. Application 2076 — Wetlands application for the installation of a new drainage pipe approximately 495' ft. in 
length from Collins Road to a north-west stream at 87 Collins Rd — Lot 51B; Lot 50 — Collins Rd & Lot 147 
— Stafford Ave; Assessor's Map 53, Lots 50, 51B, and 147; City of Bristol — Department of Public Works, 
applicant.
Bristol Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency Regular Meeting of September 2nd, 2026 
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
 
 
 
 
– 4 – 
 
 
 
The Agency received the following items in their electronic packets: 
a. Assessor’s Map with Inland Wetlands Watercourse Layers 
b. Application (with Attachment A of property owners) 
c. Plan (Electronic Copy Only) 
 
 
MOTION: Move to receive Application #2076. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Robinson 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Jarboe, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
 
The application is received.  
 
 
MOTION: Move to declare Application #2076 a significant activity and hold a public hearing with a site walk 
on September 16th at 5:00 pm.   
 
By: Robinson Seconded: Massaro 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Bridges, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application was declared a significant activity. 
 
 
 
6. Public Hearings 
 
There were no public hearings. 
 
 
 
7. Old Business 
 
a. Application #26-466F-317 — Floodplain Application for the addition to a home at 15 Hardwick Road; 
Assessor's Map 45, Lot 53; R-15 (Single-Family Residential) zone; Debora Franklin, owner; Guarantee 
Construction Services, LLC, applicant. 
 
The Agency received the following items in their electronic packets: 
a. Assessor’s Map with Inland Wetlands Watercourse Layers 
b. Application 
c. Various GIS and Aerial Maps 
 
 
MOTION: Move to open Application #26-466F-317. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Robinson
Bristol Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency Regular Meeting of September 2nd, 2026 
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
 
 
 
 
– 5 – 
 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Jarboe, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
 
Debora Franklin, 15 Hardwick Rd., the applicant, stated they are planning an addition of a closet and bathroom for 
the master bedroom. 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, stated that her contractor had submitted a preliminary drawing 
at the previous meeting that doesn’t even address the commissions concerns. A plan prepared by a surveyor is 
needed. I recommend the commission deny the application without prejudice. There is also an issue that’s unclear if 
the city received payment of $50 for the application.  
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works asked Mr. Smith if he submitted the mapping that was requested 
at the last meeting.  
Gary Smith, Guarantee Construction Services, LLC, 88 Obtuse Hill Rd., stated that it took a while to locate an 
engineer. Stated he paid the fees. 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., stated the application has been active since, you know, July. There is a time limit. Once 
again, I would propose that the Commission deny the application without prejudice. You certainly have the right to 
resubmit. I would even, subject to the fact if they paid for this application, I would waive the application fee. You can 
simply come back next month. 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
 
MOTION: Move to deny Floodplain Application #26-466F-317 without prejudice, and waive the payment if the 
applicant can prove that the list application fee was paid. 
By: Massaro        Seconded: Robinson 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Bridges, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is denied. 
 
 
8. New Business 
 
None 
 
 
 
 
9. Staff Reports  
 
a. IWWA Report – July 2026 and August 2026
Bristol Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency Regular Meeting of September 2nd, 2026 
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
 
 
 
 
– 6 – 
 
 
 
The Agency received the following items in their electronic packets: 
 
a. Inland Wetlands Enforcement Officer report, dated June 30, 2026, from Zachary Norton, Zoning 
Enforcement Officer, (Environmental Protection Technician) 
 
b. Inland Wetlands Enforcement Officer report, dated August 28, 2026, from Zachary Norton, Zoning 
Enforcement Officer, (Environmental Protection Technician 
 
 
 
MOTION Move to file the reports from the Inland Wetlands Zoning Enforcement Officer. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Massaro 
 
For: Klimek, Valentino, Duquette, Jarboe, Massaro, and Rooks. 
Against: Robinson 
Abstained: None. 
 
The reports are filed. 
 
Commissioner Robinson voiced concerns with the cease and correct on Grassy Road.
Bristol Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency Regular Meeting of September 2nd, 2026 
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
 
 
 
 
– 7 – 
 
 
 
10. Communications 
 
None 
 
11. Conservation Topics 
 
 
There were no Conservation Topics 
 
 
12. Adjournment 
 
 
MOTION: Move to adjourn at 7:07 P.M. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Robinson 
 
For: Duquette, Klimek, Valentino, Bridges, Massaro, Robinson and Rooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
 
 
 
 
This meeting was recorded. 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Janet Little 
 
 
 
David Rooks, Chairman Daniel Massaro, Jr., Secretary 
Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency  
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol
